import unittest
from doorstop import Doorstop

class TestDoorstopRequirements(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_store_requirements(self):
        # Create a new Doorstop instance
        ds = Doorstop()

        # Create a new requirement
        req = ds.create_requirement("REQ-001", "This is a requirement")

        # Store the requirement
        ds.store_requirement(req)

        # Verify that the requirement is stored permanently
        stored_req = ds.read_requirement("REQ-001")
        self.assertEqual(stored_req.key, "REQ-001")
        self.assertEqual(stored_req.text, "This is a requirement")

    def test_change_management(self):
        # Create a new Doorstop instance
        ds = Doorstop()

        # Create a new requirement
        req = ds.create_requirement("REQ-001", "This is a requirement")

        # Store the requirement
        ds.store_requirement(req)

        # Change the requirement
        req.text = "This is a new requirement"
        ds.store_requirement(req)

        # Verify that the requirement has been changed
        stored_req = ds.read_requirement("REQ-001")
        self.assertEqual(stored_req.key, "REQ-001")
        self.assertEqual(stored_req.text, "This is a new requirement")

    def test_associate_requirements_changes(self):
        # Create a new Doorstop instance
        ds = Doorstop()

        # Create a new requirement
        req = ds.create_requirement("REQ-001", "This is a requirement")

        # Store the requirement
        ds.store_requirement(req)

        # Change the requirement
        req.text = "This is a new requirement"
        ds.store_requirement(req)

        # Verify that the requirement change is associated with a developer
        stored_req = ds.read_requirement("REQ-001")
        self.assertEqual(stored_req.key, "REQ-001")
        self.assertEqual(stored_req.text, "This is a new requirement")
        self.assertIsNotNone(stored_req.change_date)
        self.assertIsNotNone(stored_req.change_user)

    def test_scalability(self):
        # Create a new Doorstop instance
        ds = Doorstop()

        # Create 1000 new requirements
        for i in range(1000):
            req = ds.create_requirement(f"REQ-{i+1}", f"This is requirement {i+1}")
            ds.store_requirement(req)

        # Verify that the requirements are stored
        for i in range(1000):
            stored_req = ds.read_requirement(f"REQ-{i+1}")
            self.assertEqual(stored_req.key, f"REQ-{i+1}")
            self.assertEqual(stored_req.text, f"This is requirement {i+1}")

    def test_lightweight_installation(self):
        # Create a new Doorstop instance
        ds = Doorstop()

        # Measure the memory usage before installation
        import psutil
        mem_before = psutil.virtual_memory().percent

        # Install Doorstop
        ds.install()

        # Measure the memory usage after installation
        mem_after = psutil.virtual_memory().percent

        # Verify that the memory usage has not increased significantly
        self.assertLessEqual(mem_after - mem_before, 10)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
